subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should the TUI fix disruptive scroll jumps through OpenClaw-owned viewport/follow state, a pi-tui renderer fix or patch, or a new explicit TUI auto-scroll setting?
rationale: The source path is credible, but the durable fix crosses terminal UX policy, dependency ownership, and possible settings-surface expansion rather than being a narrow code-only repair.

options.title: Repair renderer and anchoring
options.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that stops content-driven redraws from clearing or jumping terminal scrollback, then auto-follow only when the user is already at the tail.

options.title: Add a TUI auto-scroll setting
options.body: Expose an explicit terminal preference if maintainers want user control, accepting the added settings surface and fresh/upgrade proof burden.

options.title: Hold for live repro first
options.body: Keep the issue open without implementation until a current-main PTY capture demonstrates the exact jump and renderer reason.

recommendation.title: Repair renderer and anchoring
recommendation.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that stops content-driven redraws from clearing or jumping terminal scrollback, then auto-follow only when the user is already at the tail.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent TUI state and event-handler history makes vincentkoc the strongest routing candidate for deciding the TUI-owned part of the fix shape.
